examples.ko: 현실과 괴리된 정책은 별 도움이 안 돼요.
examples.en: A policy detached from reality is not much help.

examples.ko: 이상이 현실과 너무 괴리돼서 실현하기 어려워요.
examples.en: The ideal is so far from reality that it is hard to achieve.

examples.ko: 요즘 뉴스는 서민의 삶과 괴리돼 보여요.
examples.en: The news these days seems out of touch with ordinary people's lives.

examples.ko: 말과 행동이 괴리되면 사람들이 믿지 않아요.
examples.en: If words and actions are at odds, people won't trust you.

examples.ko: 현장과 괴리되지 않도록 직접 가서 확인해요.
examples.en: I go and check in person so as not to lose touch with the field.
My thinking gradually became detached from reality.

explain: '현실과 괴리되다'처럼 '~와/과'와 함께 써요. 정책, 이론, 생각이 실제와 떨어져 있다고 비판할 때 자주 나와요. 말할 때보다 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used with '~와/과', as in '현실과 괴리되다'. It often appears when criticizing a policy, theory or idea for being out of touch with reality. It is more common in writing and news than in speech.

examples.en: This book is divided into three parts.
They are clothes that are easy to tell apart by color.
The two words are distinguished by how they're used.
The trash is sorted by type.
You can't tell them apart from appearance alone.
Work goes smoothly when public and private are kept separate.

explain: '~으로 구분되다'는 여러 부분으로 나뉘는 것, '~와 구분되다'는 다른 것과 달라서 알아볼 수 있는 것이에요. 비슷한 '구별되다'는 차이를 알아보는 쪽에 더 가까워요. 책이나 목록을 나눌 때는 구분되다를 자주 써요.
explain_en: ~으로 구분되다 means being divided into parts, and ~와 구분되다 means being told apart from something else. 구별되다 leans more toward noticing a difference. For splitting books or lists, 구분되다 is common.

examples.en: Grandfather is laughing heartily watching TV.
The guests roared with laughter at a single joke.
The men sit around talking and laughing loudly.
Father was in a good mood and laughing all day.

examples.ko: 너무 껄껄거리지 말고 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't guffaw so much and keep it down.
The sound of loud laughter reaches the hallway.

explain: '껄껄 웃다'를 한 동사로 말한 거예요. '-거리다'는 같은 동작이 이어진다는 느낌이 있어서 계속 크게 웃는 모습에 어울려요. 윗사람이 웃을 때는 '껄껄거리셨어요'처럼 높여요.
explain_en: It is '껄껄 웃다' packed into one verb. '-거리다' gives a feel of continued action, so it suits ongoing loud laughter. For someone senior, use the honorific form, like '껄껄거리셨어요'.

examples.en: The ducks quack on the pond all day long.

examples.ko: 그렇게 꽥꽥거리지 말고 차분히 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't yell like that; try speaking calmly.

examples.ko: 옆집 아이가 복도에서 꽥꽥거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The kid next door was screaming in the hallway, so I couldn't sleep.
Why are you yelling only at me since this morning?

examples.ko: 시장에서 아저씨가 꽥꽥거리며 물건을 팔고 있어요.
examples.en: A man at the market is shouting as he sells his goods.
My friend screamed when he saw his test result.

explain: 오리 소리에도 쓰지만, 사람이 시끄럽게 소리를 지를 때 쓰면 '왜 저렇게 시끄럽게 굴어' 하는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '소리치다'보다 거칠게 들리니까 남에게 직접 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요. 비슷하게 '꽥꽥대다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for ducks, but when applied to people it sounds negative, as if they are being noisy and annoying. It sounds harsher than '소리치다', so saying it directly to someone can be rude. '꽥꽥대다' is a similar word.

examples.en: I tied the string loosely, so it keeps coming undone.

examples.ko: 나사를 느슨히 조이면 흔들릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you tighten the screw only loosely, it may wobble.
I tied my hair loosely and sat down comfortably.
Nowadays the rules are being applied loosely.

examples.ko: 줄을 느슨히 잡으면 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you hold the rope loosely, you might drop it.

examples.ko: 마음을 느슨히 먹으면 일이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you let your guard down, things don't go well.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '느슨하게'라고도 말해요. 반대말은 '팽팽히'나 '단단히'이고, 끈·나사처럼 물건뿐 아니라 규칙이나 마음가짐이 풀린 것에도 써요.
explain_en: In everyday speech people also say '느슨하게'. Its opposites are '팽팽히' and '단단히', and it applies not only to things like strings and screws but also to relaxed rules or attitudes.

en: invincibility; being unbeaten; being without any failure

examples.ko: 그 팀은 홈경기에서 불패 기록을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: That team is keeping up its unbeaten record in home games.

examples.ko: 이 감독은 시즌 내내 불패를 자랑했어요.
examples.en: This manager boasted of being unbeaten all season.
The saying 'real estate never loses' is now a thing of the past.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 열 경기째 불패 행진 중이에요.
examples.en: Our team is on a ten-game unbeaten streak.

examples.ko: 불패의 에이스가 드디어 첫 패배를 당했어요.
examples.en: The undefeated ace finally suffered his first loss.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 선거에서 불패 신화를 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: That candidate kept up the myth of never losing an election.

explain: '불패 신화', '불패 행진'처럼 정해진 말과 함께 자주 써요. 스포츠 기사나 경제 뉴스 제목에서 '○○ 불패'라고 많이 보여요. 반대로 지는 것은 '패배'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is usually paired with set words like '불패 신화' and '불패 행진'. You often see '○○ 불패' in sports and economic news headlines. The opposite, losing, is '패배'.

examples.ko: 그 가게의 영업 행태가 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The way that shop does business became a problem.

examples.ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들의 소비 행태를 조사했어요.
examples.en: We surveyed the spending patterns of young people these days.

examples.ko: 운전 중에 휴대폰을 보는 행태는 위험해요.
examples.en: Looking at a phone while driving is dangerous behavior.
If this kind of behavior continues, you lose trust.
I observed the behavior of animals for a long time.
The employees protested against the company's unfair conduct.

explain: '행동'은 한 번의 움직임에도 쓰지만, '행태'는 반복되는 모습이나 방식을 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '소비 행태', '영업 행태'처럼 많이 쓰고, 좋지 않은 모습을 말할 때가 많아요. 칭찬할 때는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: '행동' can describe a single action, but '행태' is for a repeated pattern or way of behaving. It appears in phrases like '소비 행태' (spending pattern) and '영업 행태' (business practice), and often points to something undesirable. It is rarely used for praise.
